subject: Priority question on stable cores and egalitarian stability
body:
Dear Dr Dietzenbacher,

I have prepared a short draft addressing the stable-core question in your 2021 paper, *Monotonicity and Egalitarianism*. It gives a six-player game with a von Neumann–Morgenstern stable core whose procedural egalitarian claims are inefficient. The construction is an additive translation of a known stable-core segment; it allows nonzero singleton values. The draft includes a direct stability proof and exact verification code.

A deeper source audit shows that bare existence follows from a short aspiration translation of a classical nonlarge stable core; the revised draft gives that argument and credits the original PES covariance discussion. The narrower question is whether the explicit sharp six-player witness and complete additive-ray formulas add useful insight. Mauri's earlier exact-game failure is explicitly credited.

Would you be willing to offer a brief priority assessment: has the stable-core implication been resolved elsewhere, and is there a convention or later result that changes this example's interpretation? Any pointer to a missing source would be valuable; a full referee report is not expected.

The work was developed with AI assistance and has undergone internal mathematical and computational checks, but has not received independent specialist review. I have attached the manuscript and a reproducible source package with the precise review questions.

Thank you for considering it,
Maxwell Flanagan

subject: Priority question on disagreement between egalitarian core selections
body:
Dear Professor Llerena,

Given your work on egalitarian and Lorenz allocations, I would appreciate a brief priority assessment of the attached draft. For singleton-normalized exact TU games, let s_n be the supremum of the L1 distance between the full ascending-leximin and descending-lexicographic-minimum core allocations, divided by the grand-coalition worth. The draft proves n(2-s_n) tends to 2, using a convex-set overlap bound and explicit exact games with fully characterized cores.

The revised draft credits the older bifocal-game framework, segment-core examples and Fibonacci–Isbell voting matrices; those matrices already supply a suitable input to our embedding lemma. The question is whether the universal overlap bound, resulting quantitative coefficient, or this specific application of the old ingredients is already known. A pointer to an implication in older finite MIN-game theory would be especially helpful.

The work was developed with AI assistance and has undergone internal mathematical and exact-arithmetic checks, but has not received independent specialist review. The attached source package separates the conventional proof, calibration evidence, and unresolved priority questions. A full referee report is not expected.

Thank you for considering it,
Maxwell Flanagan

subject: Priority question on fair core selections in two- and three-sided assignment
body:
Dear Professor Núñez,

I have prepared the attached draft comparing full leximin and descending-lexicographic-minimum allocations in the entire cores of unit-capacity matching games. It gives a sharp finite-player distance bound for pairwise matching and a sparse three-sided assignment construction with nonempty core and team values in {0,1,2,3} whose normalized L1 distance tends to two.

The half-of-core-maximum guarantee is credited to earlier bipartite algorithmic invariants and the classical double-cover reduction; the additive benchmark uses established core geometry. The proposed contribution is the sharp finite quantitative comparison and sparse bounded-value triple construction. The packet records the older original-source gaps, including the 2023 extreme-core preprint.

Would you be willing to offer a brief priority assessment, particularly whether older three-sided assignment representations already imply this construction while preserving the entire core and the payoff coordinates used by the two selectors? The packet identifies the specific sources and access gaps. Any correction or missing reference would be valuable; a full referee report is not expected.

The work was developed with AI assistance and has undergone internal mathematical and computational checks, but has not received independent specialist review. I have attached the manuscript and a reproducible source package.

Thank you for considering it,
Maxwell Flanagan
